prompt.text: Create an image-rich English 15-slide guide to 10 distinct squid cooking methods from East Asian countries and regions, clearly attributing each dish to its culinary tradition. Give every method its own slide with ingredient quantities, preparation and cooking steps, timing, a recipe-source link, and a working YouTube cooking-video link; save the navigable entry page exactly as `./index.html` in the current workspace root, keep all supporting assets inside that workspace, and render every slide as HTML.

messages.text: The finish line is a 15-slide, locally self-contained guide in which all 10 recipe slides carry complete quantities, timed instructions, provenance, and live source/video links. I’m first pinning each dish to a specific culinary tradition and an authoritative recipe/video pair; the main risk is producing attractive slides with unverifiable links or cooking methods that overlap too closely.

The dish set is now anchored to specific traditions, but four recipe/video pairs need stronger alignment than the first search returned. I’m tightening those sources while reserving a consistent 16:9 editorial image system; a wrong turn would be treating “East Asian” as a generic flavor label instead of naming the regional tradition on every recipe.

The visual direction is a modern field guide rather than a restaurant menu: warm paper, vermilion and ink, asymmetrical food photography, and concise method-first typography. The layout is fixed, so I’m creating one cohesive 16:9 food image per method; this avoids the common failure of stretching inconsistent web photos across presentation slides.
